title: 1. Origin, Corporate Evolution & Past Stock Cycles
summary_box: Founded in 1983 as U.P. Glycols and renamed India Glycols Limited in 1986, the Bhartia family's Kashipur complex pioneered industrial-scale bio-based Monoethylene Glycol (MEG) in 1989. Across four decades, the business cycled from debt-heavy petrochemical-spread busts (FY15–FY16 losses) to a 2021 Clariant JV carve-out. Management followed with a ₹467 Cr preferential deleveraging in November 2025 and a three-way demerger effective September 1, 2026. Listed INDIAGLYCO now stands as a pure-play green specialty chemicals and industrial gases platform.

epigraph.quote: A conglomerate is often a greenhouse that shelters a fragile seedling—until the day comes when the trees must be planted in separate soil to see which ones can bear their own weight.
epigraph.author: Industrial Capital Allocation Maxim

web_blocks.html: To understand India Glycols Limited (INDIAGLYCO) today, you must look past the surface shock of its latest quarterly income statement. In Q1 FY27 (ended June 2026) and Q2 FY27 (ended September 2026), consolidated sales printed ₹357 Cr and ₹362 Cr. That looked like a 66% and 67% year-on-year collapse from ₹1,040 Cr in Q1 FY26 and ₹1,092 Cr in Q2 FY26 [1][21]. A superficial screen would flag a business in freefall. In reality, those numbers mark the birth of a completely different listed perimeter. Effective September 1, 2026 (with a retroactive Appointed Date of April 1, 2026), India Glycols executed an NCLT-sanctioned three-way demerger. It spun out its Potable Spirits & Bio-Fuels arm (IGL Spirits Limited) and its Nutraceuticals & Bio-Polymers arm (Ennature Bio Pharma Limited) [2][3][8].

The company's roots stretch back to November 19, 1983, when the Bhartia family incorporated U.P. Glycols Limited in Kashipur, Uttarakhand (then Uttar Pradesh) [18]. Operating via Vam Organic Chemicals Ltd, founder-promoter Late M.L. Bhartia and U.S. Bhartia sited the plant in the sugarcane belt. Renamed India Glycols Limited on September 4, 1986, and publicly capitalized in July 1988, the company began commercial production at Kashipur in April 1989 [18]. Its founding technological bet was audacious. Instead of cracking naphtha or natural gas to make Ethylene Oxide (EO) and Monoethylene Glycol (MEG), IGL fermented sugarcane molasses into ethanol. It then dehydrated that ethanol into ethylene and oxidized it into 100% bio-based MEG and EO [10][18].

That green-chemistry moat came with a structural curse that defined IGL's first three decades. Its input costs were tied to Indian agricultural cycles, specifically sugarcane molasses and later grain. By contrast, its selling prices for commodity bio-MEG followed global petrochemical MEG benchmarks driven by crude oil and Middle Eastern or Chinese naphtha crackers [17]. When crude oil collapsed in FY15–FY16, global MEG prices plunged. Margins collapsed just as debt from multi-year expansions peaked at ₹2,264 Cr in March 2015 [1][17]. IGL posted consecutive net losses of -₹89 Cr in FY15 and -₹57 Cr in FY16, while promoter share encumbrances rose past 80% during the stress cycle [1][17].

Rather than staying trapped in commodity glycols, management (led by CMD U.S. Bhartia and CEO Rupark Sarswat) engineered a multi-stage pivot across 2017–2026 [1][11][12]. First, IGL scaled its high-margin UP and Uttarakhand Potable Spirits franchise and built grain-based distilleries for India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) [13]. Second, on June 30, 2021, IGL carved out its Bio-EO specialty chemicals unit at Kashipur via a ₹652.22 Cr slump sale into a 51:49 joint venture with Switzerland's Clariant International (Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals Pvt Ltd). That transaction booked a ₹239.88 Cr exceptional gain in FY22, pushing FY22 Other Income to ₹260 Cr and Net Profit to ₹340 Cr, and prepaid high-cost NBFC term loans [1][11]. Third, in November 2025, IGL completed a ₹466.99 Cr preferential share allotment (5.10 million shares, backed by promoter entity Kashipur Holdings Ltd and non-promoter institutions) to cut debt ahead of the demerger [15].

web_blocks.caption: Four Decades of Corporate Evolution & Business Cycles (1983–2026)
rows: 1983–1989: Founding
Incorporated as U.P. Glycols (1983); renamed IGL (1986); Kashipur bio-MEG commissioned (1989).
Established global first-mover status in molasses-route bio-MEG & bio-EO [18].
Green feedstock is a differentiator, but commodity MEG pricing still tracks crude.
2010–2016: Capex & Bust
Debt-funded expansion met crude oil & petrochemical MEG price crash.
Borrowings peaked at ₹2,264 Cr (FY15); Net Losses of -₹89 Cr (FY15) and -₹57 Cr (FY16) [1][17].
High leverage + agricultural input/crude output mismatch amplifies downturns.
2017–2021: Spirits & Clariant JV
Scaled UP/Uttarakhand spirits; June 2021 slump sale of Bio-EO unit into 51:49 Clariant JV.
FY22 Other Income spiked to ₹260 Cr (₹239.88 Cr exceptional gain); prepaid term debt [1][11].
Partnering with a global specialty leader monetized bio-EO without solo balance-sheet strain.
2022–2025: Ethanol & Equity Raise
Expanded Kashipur & Gorakhpur grain distilleries; ₹466.99 Cr preferential issue (Nov 2025).
FY26 Sales hit ₹4,211 Cr, OP ₹649 Cr; promoter pledge cleared to Nil [1][15][16].
Heavy capex kept FCF negative (-₹391 Cr FY25, -₹47 Cr FY26) until equity infusion.
Apr–Sep 2026: Three-Way Demerger
NCLT approved split (Jul 17, 2026); Effective Sep 1, 2026; Appointed Date Apr 1, 2026.
Spirits/Bio-Fuels (1:1) & Ennature (1:3) exited; Borrowings halved ₹1,691 Cr → ₹826 Cr [1][2][3].
Listed INDIAGLYCO is now a cleaner, lower-debt BSPC + Industrial Gases + 49% JV entity.
web_blocks.takeaway: Every major value-crystallizing inflection at India Glycols came from separating capital-intensive commodity assets from specialized, partner-backed, or consumer-facing verticals.

web_blocks.mechanism: Pioneered bio-fermentation routes for specialty molecules (farnesene, squalane) from sugarcane, betting that sustainability-conscious consumer brands would pay durable green premiums over petrochemical substitutes while funding multi-hundred-million-dollar plant capex with debt.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Accumulated over $1.2B in debt and cumulative losses; negative free cash flow persisted as fermentation scale-up costs exceeded specialty pricing power, culminating in Chapter 11 filing in August 2023.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Green chemistry alone does not guarantee compounding. When bio-based manufacturing requires heavy fixed assets and faces fossil-route price ceilings, surviving depends on exiting low-margin volume, securing take-or-pay/JV partners (like Clariant), and keeping net debt conservative.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Across India Glycols' 40-year arc, the key discipline is separating optical revenue shrinkage from structural balance-sheet healing. A naive reader seeing -67% YoY sales in September 2026 assumes catastrophe. A forensic reader sees that ₹865 Cr of debt and two distinct businesses moved to shareholders via separate share certificates.

Yet the history also warns us against romanticizing bio-based chemicals. In 2015–2016, the exact same Kashipur complex lost money because sugarcane molasses did not fall as fast as crude-linked MEG. Post-demerger INDIAGLYCO must now prove it can earn above its cost of capital without the ~21% EBIT-margin Potable Spirits cushion.

book_paragraphs: Imagine standing at the gates of India Glycols' 300-acre integrated complex in Kashipur, Uttarakhand, in the spring of 1989. Around you lie the sugarcane fields of the Terai belt, and inside the perimeter towers a chemical plant attempting something no other facility on earth had commercialized at scale: turning agricultural molasses into Monoethylene Glycol, the building block of polyester fibers and PET bottles, without touching a drop of crude oil.

For you and me studying this business nearly four decades later, that origin story explains both its enduring pride and its recurring vulnerability. Late M.L. Bhartia and U.S. Bhartia built a genuine technological moat in bio-based ethylene oxide, yet for thirty years the stock market treated India Glycols as a leveraged cyclical because its selling prices were dictated by Middle Eastern naphtha crackers while its raw material costs followed Indian monsoon and sugarcane politics.

The reckoning arrived in FY2015 and FY2016. Borrowings had climbed to ₹2,264 Cr just as global crude oil crashed, dragging petrochemical MEG prices down with it. India Glycols bled ₹89 Cr in FY15 and ₹57 Cr in FY16, and promoter share pledges swelled past 80%. Most commodity chemical companies in that position either dilute equity at distressed terms or stagnate for a decade. Instead, India Glycols spent the next ten years methodically unbundling itself.

First came the 2021 Clariant joint venture, where India Glycols sold its Bio-EO specialty unit for ₹652.22 Cr into a 51:49 partnership with Switzerland's Clariant, booking a ₹239.88 Cr exceptional gain and retiring expensive NBFC debt. Then came the ₹466.99 Cr preferential equity raise in November 2025, wiping out promoter share pledges to zero. Finally, on September 1, 2026—retroactive to April 1, 2026—the NCLT-approved three-way demerger split the conglomerate into IGL Spirits Limited, Ennature Bio Pharma Limited, and the residual India Glycols Limited.

That is why the September 2026 quarterly table looks like a cliff edge—sales dropping from ₹1,092 Cr to ₹362 Cr—when in truth it is a surgical amputation of two healthy limbs that were given their own legs to walk on. Our job in the chapters ahead is to examine the torso that remains.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Every conglomerate demerger forces you to ask a blunt question: did management spin off the crown jewels and leave the problem child behind, or did it create three focused businesses that can each allocate capital cleanly? Keep that question front and center as we dissect the segments in Chapter 2.
